text:
devin: RFC follow-up — proposal to replace fixed window counters with per-tenant sliding-credit (exp-decay) tracked at the admission shim. want quick sanity-check on interface surface and rollout plan.
anya: sounds promising. main win is smoother burst absorption, right?
kevin: yes, but storage + reconciliation is my worry. how do we recover if credit drift happens across routers/regions?
sophie: we can keep a compact vector clock and last-update ts with each credit blob; routers reconcile with a 'merge by max-ts' rule, then run a bounded repair sweep. tradeoffs: slightly more metadata, but avoids global locks.
devin: proposal for contract between admission-controller and router: 1) router sends tenant_id + requested_units 2) admission responds with {granted_units, remaining_credit, decay_half_life_ms} 3) router attaches remaining_credit to in-flight context so downstream can re-evaluate on retries.
kevin: interface looks ok. question: should admission expose an estimated p99-penalty probability so routers can switch to low-latency fallback earlier? or keep heuristic purely on remaining_credit?
anya: i'd avoid probabilistic signals in the first rollout. two-phase: start with credits + decay params, gather telemetry, then add optional 'pressure_score' later.
sophie: agreed. also add an 'abort_budget' field for latency-sensitive routes so callers know a safe retry budget. e.g. abort_budget=2 means up to 2 client retries before backoff.
devin: included a tiny config sketch we can use in the simulator:
```json
{
  "policy": "sliding_credit_v1",
  "decay_half_life_ms": 300000,
  "min_repair_interval_s": 60,
  "abort_budget_per_route": {"chat": 1, "completion": 2}
}
```
kevin: can we also ship a simulator job that replays 30 days of real traffic and compares p95 latency & error-rate between fixed-window and sliding-credit? i'll run that if folks tag datasets.
anya: tagging datasets now. i'll add a synthetic spike scenario too (:zap:).
sophie: operational concerns: need a small audit log entry whenever remaining_credit < threshold for high-tier tenants. plus a fast path to force-reset credits for debugging. ops-bot: noted — will create alert template and a runbook stub.
devin: rollout plan suggestion: 1) feature flag in admission (log-only) 2) shadow routers for 2 weeks 3) gradual enable on 10% then 50% 4) guardrails: automatic revert if p95 latency increases >5% or error-rate increases >0.5%.
kevin: sounds safe. action items: @anya add simulator scenarios, @kevin implement merge-and-repair prototype, @sophie draft runbook + alert, @devin wire up feature-flag gating. i'll follow up with a quick design doc.
anya: on it.
ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-8142 for runbook + alerts (link: https://tracker/redwood/INFRA-8142)
